name: Output channel cell
question: Approve one output-switch cell, laid out round U701 and copied to U601 and U801?
why_now:
Each TPS2HCS08A-Q1 drives two outputs and has 21 parts round it. The annealer placed the three channels differently. Channel 3-4 came out close to TI's layout, but in channels 1-2 and 5-6 the current-sense parts were 12 to 38 mm from their SNS pin, which makes the current reading noisy. The fault line from U801 was also caged: no track could leave pin 12.

The cell is U701's, tidied, then copied to the other two switches by reference. Only the anchors and one test point differ.

facts.label: TI layout rules
facts.value: RSNS and CSNS close to the SNS pin; CVBB1 as close as possible to the VBB and GND pins; exposed pad on a large pour with a VBB plane inside the board (In4 here); MCU signals to a via and an inner layer

facts.label: Cell
facts.value: U701 and its 21 parts (7 caps, 7 resistors, the NTC, 6 test points); 13 core, 8 flex (the NTC divider and filter and the test points, up to 4 mm; the GND probe loop up to 12 mm)

facts.label: U601
facts.value: turned from 180° to 90° and moved 4.3 mm, to (87.5, 109.4), so it matches U701's cell

facts.label: U801
facts.value: moved from (220.0, 112.1) to (224.0, 113.0). FLT pin 12 was caged at the annealer's pose and at (220, 112); here the reachability check passes it

facts.label: TP806 (GND probe loop)
facts.value: the copied pose overlapped the J908 header, so it sits at (231, 107.75), 9.4 mm from pin 1

facts.label: Small fixes in all three cells
facts.value: RSNS (R605/R705/R805) 0.1 mm off the switch's courtyard; C803 0.3 mm off J908's courtyard

facts.label: Top side
facts.value: CVBB1 (C601/C701/C801) and the VDD decap (C603/C703/C803) are on F.Cu directly over their pins, as the project puts every decap on top; the rest of the cell is on B.Cu with the switch

facts.label: The one open pin
facts.value: U501 pin 29 (3V3_MAIN), between the unused pin 28 and the T1S pair on 30-31, at 0.5 mm pitch. It reads PASSABLE, so a route exists. The fan-out gives it a stub; the bulk pass then rips all of 3V3_MAIN to make room and restores 67 of its 68 connections, not this one. 3V3_MAIN has endpoints in the moved output cells (R601/R701/R801, R607/R707/R807), so the composed board changes that net's routing order; the PHY's parts did not move. Carried to the final gate as its own row

options.name: One cell, copied three times
options.summary: U701's cell, with U601 turned and U801 moved so all three are identical. The sense parts sit by the SNS pin in every channel.

images.caption: Channel 1-2 (U601), bottom side seen from above. Dashed outlines and arrows show where each part was; most came from 10–15 mm east
Channel 3-4 (U701), the cell the others copy. Only RSNS (R705) and CSNS (C704) moved, each by about 1 mm, onto the SNS pin
Channel 5-6 (U801): the cell moved 4 mm east; CSNS came from 38 mm west, and TP806 sits top right, clear of J908
TI SLVSHR0 Figure 9-5, the layout example

measures.label: RSNS to SNS pin, pad gap (all three)
CSNS to SNS pin, pad gap (all three)
CVBB1 over the VBB pad (all three)
OUT pins to header, centre to centre (1/2, 3/4, 5/6)
Fast route of the composed board (KRT / board rules)
measures.value: 1 open / 1 open: U501 pin 29 (3V3_MAIN), at the PHY. 0 in the output channels: all 12 OUT, SNS and FLT nets routed

gains: The same cell three times, each with its sense parts by the SNS pin, so the three channels read current alike
U801's fault line can be routed
costs: U601 and U801 moved, so their neighbours were checked again (the board stays buildable, 0 floorplan errors)

options.name: As the annealer left them
options.summary: Keep the three channels as on main.

images.caption: The dashed outlines are the annealer's poses

costs: Two channels with sense parts far from their pin, and one fault line that cannot be routed

recommendation.why: It meets TI's placement rules in all three channels and makes every fault line routable.

answer: Reply with A or B, or a change.
sources: TI TPS2HCS08-Q1 datasheet SLVSHR0, §9.4.1 and Figure 9-5
